The evaluation
Profit target

Reach 6% profit while following all the rules. Your account then has a final review, and once approved you become a funded trader. There's no time limit and no minimum number of trading days.

Consistency rule

Your best day can't make up more than your chosen percentage of total profit: 30%, 40% or 50%. If it does, you're not breached. You just keep trading until your best day falls below the limit.

Example: on $50K with 40% consistency and a $2,000 best day, you need at least $5,000 total profit to pass.

Funded Zero accounts have no consistency rule.

Drawdown in the evaluation

End-of-day (EOD) trailing: your loss limit moves up only when you set a new highest end-of-day closing balance. It doesn't follow unrealised profit during the day.

Intraday trailing: your loss limit follows your highest equity in real time, including open profit.

Either way, the limit never moves down, and hitting it is a hard breach.

Daily loss limit (if chosen)

If you chose an account with a daily loss limit, hitting it is a soft breach: open trades are closed, trading locks for the rest of the day, and it unlocks at the 5:00 PM New York rollover. The account isn't failed. The same limit carries into your funded account.

Zero FAQs
How is Zero different from Reserve?

Both have the same profit target, drawdown sizes and contract limits. Zero pays out daily with no cap once you clear your buffer, uses an intraday drawdown when funded, and lets you choose your evaluation drawdown type and a 30%, 40% or 50% consistency rule. Reserve pays up to 50% of profit after 5 winning days, with a cap per payout.

Which option should I pick?

End-of-day drawdown gives you more room during the day, because it ignores open profit until the close. A daily loss limit and a stricter consistency rule lower the price. Pick the mix that suits how you trade.

Can I change my options after buying?

No. Your options are set at checkout and stay with the account.

Can I reset a Zero account?

You can reset a breached evaluation from your dashboard, at the evaluation's current sale price. Funded Zero accounts can't be reset.

Does the daily loss limit fail my account?

No. It's a soft breach. Trading locks for the rest of the day and unlocks at the 5:00 PM New York rollover.

Can I trade the news?

Yes during the evaluation. Once you're funded, news trading isn't allowed.

How fast can I get paid?

Once your balance is above the buffer, you can request a payout every day. Requests are processed within 24 business hours. See How payouts work.

What happens if I make $8,000 in one day?

That account is closed and we email you with two options: take a $3,600 payout for each account that hit $8,000, followed by a 30-day cooldown; or move to Live with a Live Bonus for each funded Zero account. Profit above $8,000 that day isn't kept.

How many Zero accounts can I have?

Up to 5 funded Zero accounts at a time, of any size.

Which platform can I use?

Zero is available on NinjaTrader.

How often you need to trade to keep CFD and Futures accounts active, and when the inactivity period starts.

Applies to:
CFD and Futures
Updated 17 November 2026
Short answer

Place at least one trade within your account's inactivity period. If you don't, the account is treated as inactive and breached.

Inactivity periods

Account

	

Trade at least once every




CFD: all accounts

	

30 days




Futures: evaluation accounts

	

10 calendar days




Futures: funded accounts upgraded on or after 10 October 2026

	

10 calendar days

7 calendar days

When does the clock start?

CFD: the inactivity period counts from the moment the account is created, even though your evaluation itself only starts with your first trade. If you buy an account, don't leave it untouched for more than 30 days.

Keep an eye on your account activity in the dashboard, especially on funded Futures accounts, where the period is much shorter.

How Blue Guardian works

How evaluations, funded accounts and instant accounts work for CFD and Futures, what happens when you pass, and the Trader Agreement.

Applies to:
CFD and Futures
Updated 15 November 2026
Short answer

Choose an evaluation and reach its profit target while following the rules to earn a funded account, or buy an instant account and start funded straight away. Once funded, you keep a share of the profits you make.

The path most traders follow. Instant accounts skip the evaluation and pass steps.
CFD accounts

Evaluations: 1 Step Nano, 1 Step Standard, 2 Step Standard, 2 Step Nano and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL). Pass your evaluation and a funded account is issued.

Instant accounts: Instant Standard and Instant Starter give you a funded account immediately, with no evaluation.

Account sizes: $5K, $10K, $25K, $50K, $100K, $200K, $300K and $400K. The size is the balance you trade with.

Futures accounts

One-phase evaluation: Zero, Elite and Reserve accounts use a single evaluation phase. Reach the profit target while following the rules, and your account is reviewed and then funded. Zero lets you choose your drawdown type, daily loss limit and consistency rule at checkout, and pays out daily once funded.

Direct (instant funding): start on a funded account immediately, with no evaluation.

Express: no longer available to buy from 16 November 2026. Existing Express accounts keep their rules.

Account sizes: $25K, $50K, $100K and $150K.

One-time fee: every Futures account is a single purchase. There are no monthly subscriptions, renewal fees or activation fees when you get funded.

When does my evaluation start?

CFD: your evaluation starts with your first trade. The inactivity rule, however, counts from the moment the account is created, so don't leave a new account untouched for more than 30 days.

I passed. What happens next?

CFD: within 6–12 business hours you'll receive your funded account login details by email, together with your Trader Agreement and Funded Trader Certificate.

Futures: once you hit the profit target, your account goes through a final review. After it's approved, you move on to your funded account.

The Trader Agreement

Your relationship with Blue Guardian as a funded trader is governed by the Blue Guardian Trader Agreement. It's a legally binding contract, issued after you pass, and it must be signed before your funded account is issued.

Am I trading with real money?

CFD: no. All CFD accounts, including funded accounts, are demo accounts in a simulated environment with virtual funds. They use real market prices from liquidity providers so that trading conditions are as realistic as possible.

Futures: funded accounts start as simulated (sim) accounts. Traders can progress to a Live Account. Zero has its own route: see Zero Path to Live. For Elite, Reserve and Direct, see Elite, Reserve & Direct Path to Live.

KYC verification: what you need and when

When identity verification is required, which documents are accepted and how AML checks work. Applies to CFD and Futures.

Applies to:
CFD and Futures
Updated 13 November 2026
Short answer

You verify your identity once, before your first payout. Have a valid photo ID and a proof of address from the last 3 months ready, and be prepared to take a live selfie.

When is KYC required?

Before your first payout on a funded or instant funded account

Before your first affiliate payout

Verification is done once per person, and only one verified profile is allowed per individual.

What you'll need
1. Proof of identity

A live photo of a valid, unexpired document: passport, national ID card, driver's licence or residence permit.

Check which documents are accepted in your country: sumsub.com/supported-documents

2. Live selfie

A live selfie or short video that clearly shows your face and matches your ID.

3. Proof of address

Dated within the last 3 months and showing your full address. Any one of these:

Bank statement

Utility bill (electricity, water, internet)

Government-issued letter

Lease agreement signed by both parties

Credit card statement

Employer letter confirming your address

House purchase deed

If you have none of these, an ID document that shows your full address may be accepted. It must be a different document from the one you used as proof of identity.

How to verify

Open the Verification tab in your dashboard and follow the steps.

Complete verification on your own device and your normal internet connection. Using a virtual machine, remote desktop or proxy is not allowed and may cause verification to fail, extra checks, or payout delays.

AML screening

Every user is automatically screened against:

Global sanctions and watchlists, including OFAC, UN, HMT and EU

Politically exposed person (PEP) databases

Adverse media reports

Extra checks you may be asked for

Live KYC/AML check: during a payout review we may ask for an additional live verification, for example if documents are unclear or details don't match. This is case by case, not required for everyone.

Expired documents: your documents must stay valid. If one expires you may need to resubmit, which can delay payouts.

Good to know

Verification decisions are made by our third-party provider and cannot be overridden by Blue Guardian.

Multiple profiles are not allowed. If you created a second profile by mistake, contact support@blueguardian.com before you reach a payout or funding stage.

Account rules: ownership, devices and fair use

Account ownership, login sharing, the CID device rule, accurate information, multiple accounts and chargebacks, for CFD and Futures.

Applies to:
CFD and Futures
Updated 17 November 2026
Short answer

Your account is for you alone. It must be in your legal name, only you may log in and trade, you must only use your own devices, and everything you give us must be true. Breaking these rules can lead to account closure and a permanent ban.

Your account must be in your own name

Register with your legal name. Payouts are sent directly to the account holder, so the account holder and the payout recipient must be the same person.

Only you can trade your account

Don't share your login details or let anyone else access your account.

Don't let anyone place or manage trades for you.

Copy trading is only allowed between accounts you legally own.

If we detect someone else trading your account, it will be terminated immediately.

Use your own devices (CID rule)

Every device you use to log in has a unique device identifier, known as a CID. Our systems record the CID of every login and check whether the same device has been used for other traders' accounts.

The CID rule: you must not log in to your account from a device that has been used to log in to another trader's account, and you must not use your device to log in to anyone else's account. If the same CID appears on your account and another trader's account, this is a CID match, and the accounts are treated as linked.

This includes devices belonging to friends, family members, colleagues, trading communities, signal providers or account managers, as well as shared computers and VPS services.

What happens with a CID match

Accounts with a CID match are flagged and reviewed, usually during a payout review. Depending on the review, this can lead to:

Payout denial or disqualification

Removal of profits earned on the account

Suspension or permanent closure of the account

All decisions by our Risk Team are final.

How to stay within the rule

Only log in from your own personal phone, computer or laptop.

Never log in to someone else's account on your device, even to help them.

Don't use public, shared or work computers, or shared VPS services.

If you've ever used a device that someone else has also used to log in to their Blue Guardian account, contact support before you trade.

Give us accurate information

These are serious violations:

Fake names, fake or altered documents, or false verification details

Using someone else's identity or payment details

Trying to bypass KYC or hide who is really operating the account

Any of these can lead to an immediate hard breach, payout denial and a permanent blacklist.

Don't use multiple accounts to abuse offers

Creating multiple profiles or accounts to abuse promotions, discount codes, resets or payout conditions is not allowed. All related accounts may be closed, profits voided and the trader permanently blacklisted.

Chargebacks

Filing a dishonest chargeback, or trying to recover money fraudulently through your payment provider after receiving access, services or payouts, leads to an immediate permanent ban.

CFD: platform password

You must log in to your trading platform with the password Blue Guardian provides. Changing your platform password is not allowed.

Updated 17 November 2026
Short answer

Once your account meets its plan's payout requirements, request a payout from the Payouts tab in your dashboard. You can be paid by crypto (up to $1,000 per request) or Rise (no maximum). A 3% processing fee applies to every payout.

Before your first payout

Complete your KYC verification. It is required before any payout.

Make sure your payout details in the dashboard are correct.

To be paid through Rise (CFD and Futures), you must set up Rise before requesting a payout: create and verify your Rise account, then in your dashboard go to Settings > Payout method, add Rise as your payout method and accept the invite. Zero: the $8,000 daily profit limit

If a funded Zero account makes $8,000 net profit in a single trading day, it's closed and you choose between a $3,600 payout for each account that hit the limit (followed by a 30-day cooldown) or moving to Live with a Live Bonus. See Zero account rules and Zero Path to Live.

Reserve: winning days and net profit

The winning-day count and the net-profit requirement both reset after each approved payout. Net profit includes all profits and losses since your last approved payout. Example on a $50,000 account: $900 of profit and a $150 losing day gives $750 net profit, which meets the requirement. The net-profit rule only decides when you're eligible; you can still request up to 50% of your total profit, up to your cap.

Paying for your account: methods, card rules and refunds

Accepted payment methods, why the card must be in your name, chargebacks, and when your fee is refunded.

Applies to:
CFD and Futures
Updated 13 November 2026
Short answer

Pay by debit/credit card or cryptocurrency, using a payment method in your own name. Third-party cards are never accepted. Fees are generally not refundable, apart from the cases below.

Payment methods

We accept debit/credit cards and cryptocurrency for all account purchases.

Can I use someone else's card?

No. You must pay with a payment method that belongs to the person who owns and trades the account. These must match:

Your registered account name

The cardholder name

Your billing address

If we detect a mismatched payment method, it can lead to account termination, payout denial, refund denial or a permanent ban.

Fraud and chargebacks

We have zero tolerance for payment fraud, including unauthorised card use, chargeback abuse, payment manipulation and false payment disputes. Any of these can lead to permanent removal from the platform.

Is my fee refundable?

CFD: for accounts bought from 21 January 2026, your evaluation fee is refunded in full after your fourth payout. This doesn't apply to Instant Starter accounts. If the account is hard-breached before the fourth payout, the fee is not refunded.

Futures: Futures fees are not refundable. The one exception: if you are moved to a Live Account, you may receive a refund for your active accounts.
